children: The bloc wants Beijing to limit imports of plug-in hybrids to 15% of market share, the FT reports. It echoes a 1980s deal with Japanese carmakers but lacks the same bite. Still, as Brussels' patchwork of policies grows, Chinese exporters' rapid acceleration into Europe may stall.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin.

The European Union has requested China voluntarily cap exports of hybrid cars at 15% of market share in the bloc, the Financial Times reported on September 17, citing three people familiar with the situation.

China-made hybrids account for about a third of the EU market now, per the report. In 2025, Chinese-made cars accounted for 12% of the bloc’s plug-in electric car sales, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association.
